name: NTSC Signal — effect fixture
description: Proving fixture for the ntsc-signal Effect: the cable/decoder half of the two-stage CRT pipeline, run alone so the signal-path artifacts stay legible. The depth stage puts the real coast-bedrock photo on the backdrop plane (sharp, low aperture) and the effect re-encodes the composited frame per scanline into an NTSC composite signal (YIQ on the 3.579545 MHz subcarrier, 180° phase flip per line and frame), then decodes it back through imperfect FIR filters — so the color bleed in the rock detail, the rainbow crawl on fine texture, the right-lagging chroma, the cable ghost, and the decoder-shaped snow are emergent from the signal model, not painted on. Temporal terms (line phase, hue jitter, snow) advance on a deterministic ~30 Hz frame clock from ctx.timestamp — scrub and export agree at every frame (ADR-0012). Full-frame piece (backgroundFill). Fixture — exercises the pipeline, not held to the deliverable floors.

content.title: Every color on this screen rode a single wire — the rainbows at the edges are where the wire gave up.
content.author: NTSC COMPOSITE · 3.579545 MHZ · CH 3
